title: CRS-34 Cargo Dragon LAUNCHED — May 15 at 6:05 p.m. EDT, Booster B1096 Lands at LZ-40, Dragon C209 En Route to ISS Harmony (SpaceX's 58th Orbital Mission of 2026, 611th Booster Recovery)
detail: SpaceX successfully launched CRS-34 Cargo Dragon on May 15, 2026, at 6:05 p.m. EDT (22:05 UTC) from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station — the third launch attempt after consecutive weather scrubs on May 12 (T-4 min abort) and May 13 (T-30s abort). Falcon 9 booster B1096 (6th flight — previously flew IMAP, GPS III-9, NROL-77, Kuiper Falcon 01, and Starlink 6-87) completed a Return-to-Launch-Site landing at Landing Zone 40 (LZ-40) approximately 7.5 minutes after liftoff, marking SpaceX's 611th cumulative Falcon booster recovery. Dragon capsule C209 (6th flight — previously flew CRS-22, CRS-24, CRS-27, CRS-30, CRS-32) separated approximately 9.5 minutes into the mission and is now en route to the ISS on a ~36-hour autonomous transit. The spacecraft carries approximately 6,500 pounds (2,950 kg) of cargo for the Expedition 74 crew: time-sensitive biological science experiments, crew supplies, and hardware including materials for ongoing ISS maintenance. Dragon C209 is scheduled to autonomously dock with the ISS Harmony module's forward port at approximately 7:05 a.m. EDT on Sunday, May 17, 2026. CRS-34 is SpaceX's 58th orbital mission of 2026 and the company's 34th operational cargo resupply delivery to the ISS under the NASA CRS-2 contract. The CRS-34 capsule is scheduled to return to Earth in mid-June 2026 with a Pacific Ocean splashdown off the California coast.

title: SpaceX IPO Public S-1 Filing Window Opens May 15 — $75B Nasdaq Debut Targeting June 2026 at $1.75T+ Valuation
detail: May 15, 2026, marks the opening of the earliest possible window for SpaceX to publicly file its S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) — the public prospectus for its planned Nasdaq IPO. Under SEC rules, the company must publish its S-1 at least 15 calendar days before launching the formal investor roadshow, which is reportedly targeting the week of June 8, 2026. SpaceX filed a confidential draft S-1 with the SEC on approximately April 1, 2026 (internally codenamed 'Project Apex'), backed by 21 underwriting banks led by Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs. The company is targeting a raise of approximately $75 billion — which would be the largest IPO in U.S. history by a significant margin, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 record of $29.4 billion. Target valuation has been reported between $1.75 trillion and $2+ trillion, depending on the source. SpaceX's planned 30% retail allocation (approximately 3x the industry norm) is designed to broaden its shareholder base ahead of anticipated inclusion in the S&P 500 index following its debut. Kalshi prediction markets as of early May 2026 placed the probability of an IPO announcement by July 1 at 82% and by August 1 at 85%. The IPO window (May 15–22 for public S-1) aligns with the management roadshow week of June 8 and a June 18–30 pricing and debut target on Nasdaq. Bloomberg has reported that SpaceX's 2026 revenue — spanning Starlink (~$15.9–24B projected), government launch contracts, and commercial payloads — gives it a fundamentals base for the valuation, though market analysts have noted the P/S multiple at $1.75T+ is in high-double-digits territory unprecedented for a launch company.
